hormuz_disruption.label: Iran / Hormuz Disruption
hormuz_disruption.last_note: The strait remains at 15 percent of pre-war traffic per JPMorgan; US resumed strikes on Iran on June 26 after ceasefire violation, removing any near-term reopening catalyst and keeping the disruption thesis firmly operational.

stagflation_regime.label: Stagflation Regime
stagflation_regime.last_note: FOMC June 17 held rates and revised Q4 2026 core PCE up to 3.3 percent while GDP was trimmed to 2.2 percent, with professional forecasters now projecting Q2 headline CPI at 6.0 percent annualized, confirming a textbook stagflationary configuration.

ai_bubble_risk.label: AI Bubble Risk Q4 2026
ai_bubble_risk.last_note: Hyperscaler capex is confirmed at 725 billion dollars in 2026 with capital intensity at 45-57 percent of revenue and 100 billion in new bond issuance, creating a debt-fueled buildout that investors are pricing with CDS protection at record levels; ROI proof remains the critical missing variable.

gold_supercycle.label: Gold Supercycle
gold_supercycle.last_note: Gold at 4096 remains pinned below JPMorgan's cited 200-day moving average of approximately 4340 and the 50-day moving average of approximately 4730, with central bank net purchases collapsing to only 16 tonnes in Q1 2026 and investors described by JPMorgan as having gold on the back burner pending Iran conflict resolution.

copper_deficit.label: Structural Copper Deficit
copper_deficit.last_note: The structural concentrate deficit is real with spot treatment charges at minus 70 dollars per tonne confirming extreme tightness and a projected cumulative deficit of 3 million tonnes by 2036, but near-term demand is clouded by China refined copper demand contracting minus 8 percent YoY in Q4 2025 and JPMorgan flagging that macroeconomic risks from the Iran conflict are likely not yet fully priced in.

nuclear_renaissance.label: Nuclear Renaissance
nuclear_renaissance.last_note: The Hormuz crisis has structurally accelerated the case for domestic power independence, uranium equities are up approximately 40 percent on average in 2026, and hyperscaler power demand with grid connection wait times exceeding four years confirms nuclear as the only credible baseload solution at scale.

ALAB.note: The AI connectivity thesis remains directionally intact given confirmed 725 billion dollar hyperscaler capex driving demand for high-bandwidth interconnect, but the P/E of 92 leaves no margin for error if capital intensity starts compressing spending on non-GPU line items.

POWL.note: The power infrastructure thesis is strengthened by grid connection wait times exceeding four years cited by JLL, but the Iran war energy shock and potential demand destruction from stagflation represent a dual macro risk to industrial order books.

MOD.note: The liquid cooling thesis is validated by Schneider Electric calling direct-to-chip foundational in April 2026, but negative FCF of minus 101 million dollars at a P/E of 22.53 in a rising-rate environment with a potential October 2026 hike creates balance sheet risk.

GFS.note: The specialty node thesis lacks a near-term catalyst as GFS is not a primary beneficiary of the AI capex wave concentrated on Nvidia GPUs and custom silicon, and the valuation at P/E 31.59 is not cheap enough to own without a clear design-win acceleration.

CRDO.note: With 206 percent revenue growth and confirmed 725 billion dollar hyperscaler AI capex validating active electrical cable and optical DSP demand, CRDO remains the clearest direct beneficiary of the connectivity bottleneck inside AI data centers.

ARM.note: The AVOID thesis remains intact; at P/E 108 ARM is pricing in a decade of flawless royalty ramp across hyperscaler custom silicon at a moment when the AI capex cycle carries rising ROI risk and the Iran conflict introduces macro headwinds to end-market device demand.

S.note: SentinelOne crossed 1 billion ARR and achieved a 6 percent non-GAAP operating margin in Q4 FY26, which is genuine operational improvement, but the stock at 15.91 is down 14.7 percent over one year and the workforce cut signal has not fully cleared.

ZS.note: Zscaler reported Q3 FY2026 revenue of 850.5 million dollars up 25 percent YoY with ARR at 3.525 billion and a record 23 percent non-GAAP operating margin, materially improving the prior AVOID thesis; valuation at P/E 28.77 is now the most compelling in the sector and the prior thesis has drifted toward reconsideration.

AXON.note: AXON Q1 2026 revenue of 807 million up 34 percent with ARR at 1.5 billion confirmed the original INTACT thesis, but the signal has since been downgraded to AVOID on valuation at P/E 42.06 and FCF of only 63 million dollars, representing a thesis drift from fundamental strength to valuation overshoot where the business is excellent but the stock is priced beyond the margin of safety.

ISRG.note: Intuitive Surgical has zero debt, $4.5B cash, 23% revenue growth, and $2.3B FCF making it a genuine compounder, but at 36x forward earnings and 29.4% below highs the surgical robotics moat thesis is unchanged — the drift is purely valuation-related, not fundamental, and the stock remains a hold-not-add until the multiple contracts further.

RXRX.note: Recursion Pharmaceuticals has revenue growth of minus 56.1%, is burning $178M in FCF with negative operating margins of minus 1985%, and is 55.2% below its 52-week high — the original AI drug discovery thesis has collapsed as clinical pipeline progress has not justified the technology premium and this is now a capital destruction story with no near-term catalyst.

JEDI.note: The drone and modern warfare rearmament thesis is structurally intact given the Hormuz crisis has accelerated defense technology procurement, but at 25% below highs and with no fundamental data available for an ETF wrapper this remains a theme trade that requires a defined technical base before adding risk.

CWAN.note: Clearwater Analytics has 74.4% revenue growth and $160M FCF which is operationally compelling, but analyst targets of $24.47 to $24.55 against the current $24.35 price provide virtually zero upside consensus — at PEG of 10.24 and EV/EBITDA of 73.69 the institutional fintech thesis is fully priced with no margin of safety.

GRAB.note: Grab at $3.30 with $6.5B cash, 23.5% revenue growth, and PEG of 0.87 is the most asymmetric deep value setup in the portfolio on a pure fundamentals basis, but the stock is 50.2% below highs and the Southeast Asia super-app monetization thesis requires a specific catalyst such as a buyback announcement or profitability upgrade to unlock value — thesis intact, no trigger yet.

VRT.note: Vertiv is a direct beneficiary of the above 1 trillion dollar 2026 data center capex cycle with power constraint urgency confirmed by the Microsoft 80 billion dollar Azure backlog, but stretched valuation demands flawless execution at a time when macro uncertainty is high.

MU.note: MU led the chip stock rally on June 15 on Iran deal optimism and structural AI memory demand is intact given that memory cost inflation drove data center capex higher in Q1 2026, but the stock is cyclical and a stagflation-driven consumer slowdown could compress DRAM pricing outside the AI data center vertical.

AMD.note: AMD surged on June 15 following an analyst upgrade and the Iran deal catalyst, with the company announcing up to 2 billion pounds in UK AI investment and the MEXT memory optimization acquisition signaling a serious data center strategy, but the stock at 548.80 dollars trades at a premium that assumes continued hyperscaler GPU wallet share gains from Nvidia.
